content: The Jardine Water Purification Plant, previously known as the Central District Filtration Plant, is recognized as the largest water filtration facility in the world. It is situated at 1000 East Ohio Street, just north of Navy Pier in Chicago, Illinois. The plant sources untreated water from two water cribs located far offshore in Lake Michigan. It processes and distributes nearly one billion gallons of water daily to residents in the northern and central regions of Chicago. The construction of the plant began in the 1960s, and it became operational in 1968. Following its establishment, the Ohio Street Beach naturally formed in the bay area created by the plant. The landscaping surrounding the facility, as well as the adjacent Milton Olive Park, was designed by the renowned landscape architect Dan Kiley. Additionally, the front entrance of the plant is adorned with a sculpture titled Hymn to Water, created by Milton Horn. The southern part of Chicago receives its water supply from a separate facility, the South Water Purification Plant. Together, the Jardine and South Water Purification Plants provide clean water to approximately 5 million residents in Chicago and 118 surrounding suburbs.
